correctness.rationale: For all n≥2, the endpoint, no-consecutive-vacancy and alternating-layer lemmas are proved in RESULT.md and imply a bijection to the initial occupied layer and binary vacancy gaps. All legal original-graph token slides are exactly adjacent unequal-gap swaps; hence two exclusion-token path graphs. Exact vertices, edges, shortest distances, component median uniqueness and diameters follow by explicit counting and monotone particle moves, including z=0,z=p and n=2 boundaries. Three separate reproducible checkers passed: bitmask original ladder up to 10 rungs, independent word slides up to 18 rungs, and gap-graph all states on paths up to 8 including unique medians. The universal statement relies on combinatorial proof, not bounded tests.

The 2001 total count follows by setting the variable to one, but does not imply adjacency, components, medianity or distances. The circular-ladder proof has related alternating-gap combinatorics but its cyclic words have different boundary conditions and its published theorem only determines minimum-i-set geometry on C_n□K_2, not the two-component, all-size open ladder result. Other papers concern general or inverse reconfiguration. Thus the specific scientific claim is not a restatement or corollary of any inspected source.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 i-graph literature classifies paths and cycles and leaves a natural first Cartesian width-two seed family. This theorem determines the ENTIRE fixed-cardinality independent-domination reconfiguration spectrum for every open ladder, not an arbitrary selected size: precise two-component obstruction, exact optimal-slide distance between every reachable pair, diameter, median geometry and edge spectrum. These properties are not implied by the known 2001 Fibonacci total and are useful for rigorous reachability and path planning in constrained maximal-independent-set reconfiguration. The old unweighted total is credited and excluded from novelty.
